name: Zheng-Dao Bioelectric Axonal Frequency Bridge
description:
The Axonal Frequency Bridge operates by piggybacking encrypted signal packets onto the body's own bioelectric nervous conduction pathways, converting digital data into modulated nerve-impulse analogs that travel through the user's peripheral nervous system before being decoded at a paired receiver implant or external contact terminal. The transmission medium is the body itself — no radio frequency is emitted, no detectable electromagnetic signature escapes the skin envelope, making conventional sweep-and-scan countermeasures effectively blind to ongoing communications. Pairing two users requires a brief physical contact handshake during which the cryptographic keys are exchanged dermally.

What distinguishes the AFB from other bio-integrated comms is its layered redundancy: if one nerve pathway is severed or disrupted — by injury, stun weapons, or neural interference — the bridge automatically reroutes through alternative conduction chains within milliseconds, maintaining signal integrity even through significant physiological trauma. The experience of receiving a transmission is described as a subtle, involuntary muscle memory sensation rather than heard audio, making it nearly impossible for bystanders to detect that communication is occurring at all.

Primarily adopted by deep-cover operatives, corporate espionage assets, and high-value informants who cannot afford any detectable comms signature, the AFB has become something of a status marker in intelligence circles — a piece of kit that announces, without announcement, that its user operates in spaces where even wireless silence is a liability.

cultural_context: In GLMZ's intelligence underworld, the phrase 'running on nerve wire' has become shorthand for operating completely off-grid. Owning an AFB implies access to Zheng-Dao's gray-market surgical networks and a professional history serious enough to warrant that level of paranoia. Among street-level fixers it is aspirational — whispered about, rarely seen. Corporate counterintelligence divisions both hunt users of the device and quietly equip their own deep assets with it.
known_users: Political dissidents operating under surveillance states
story_hooks: A contact passes the players critical intelligence via AFB handshake during a crowded corporate gala — but one player realizes the data packet also contained something else, something that wasn't part of the exchange.
A Zheng-Dao surgeon who performs AFB installations is found dead; whoever killed him took his paired receiver list, meaning every asset he ever wired is now potentially compromised.
The players are hired to extract someone whose AFB has malfunctioned and is broadcasting a faint, rhythmic bioelectric pulse — not enough to decode, but enough to track.
A black-market AFB clone is circulating in the Undercroft; it transmits cleanly but also quietly logs every exchange to an unknown third-party address.
